mechaber/1:main: Further laws of the Seder. Containing 7 seifim: He should wash his hands and bless on netilat yadayim and take the matzot in the order he placed them — the broken one between the two whole ones — and grasp them in his hand and bless HaMotzi and on eating matza, and afterward break from the upper whole one and from the broken one, both of them together, and dip them in salt. {Rama: And the custom is not to dip them in salt on the first night; plain bread does not require salt.} And he should eat them while leaning, together, a kezayit from each. And if he cannot eat two olive-bulks together, he should eat that of HaMotzi first and afterward that of eating matza. And afterward he should take a kezayit of maror and submerge it entirely in charoset and not delay it inside so that the taste of its bitterness not be nullified, and for this reason he must shake the charoset off it, and bless on eating maror and eat it without leaning. And afterward he takes the third matza and breaks from it and wraps it with the maror and dips it in charoset. {Rama: And some say one should not dip it, and so it is in customs, and so I have seen practiced.} And he says in commemoration of the Temple like Hillel, and eats them together while leaning. And from when he blesses on eating matza he should not speak of matters unrelated to the meal until he eats this korekh, so that the blessing of eating matza and the blessing of eating maror apply also to this korekh.
mechaber/2:main: If he has no vegetables for the first dipping except maror, he should bless on it at the first dipping Borei peri ha'adamah and on eating maror, and at the second dipping he dips it in charoset and eats it without a blessing.
mechaber/3:main: One who swallowed matza has fulfilled his obligation; but if he swallowed maror he has not fulfilled, for we require the taste of maror and it is lacking. And even if he swallowed matza and maror as one — he has fulfilled for matza but not for maror. And if he wrapped them in bast and swallowed, he has not even fulfilled for matza, since this is not the manner of eating.
mechaber/4:main: One who ate matza unintentionally, for example, if non-Jews or thugs forced them to eat it, has fulfilled their obligation, since they were aware that the night was Passover and that they were obligated to eat matza. But if they believed that it was a regular day, or that this was not matza, they have not fulfilled their obligation.
mechaber/5:main: One who ate an olive-bulk of matza while they were overcome by a period of insanity and then later became healed is obligated to eat it after being healed, since that act of eating occurred at a time when they were exempt from all commandments.
mechaber/6:main: One who ate half an olive-bulk and later ate another half olive-bulk has fulfilled their obligation, as long as one does not pause between the two acts of eating longer than the time it takes to eat a loaf of bread. {Rama: (And see below 612:3)}
mechaber/7:main: There is no obligation to eat matza except on the first night alone. And even on the first night one fulfills with a kezayit. {Rama: And the custom is to make the three Seder matzot from an issaron, in commemoration of the loaves of the thanksgiving offering, and they make a mark on them to know which is first or second or third, and they place the first on top, the second in the middle, and the third on the bottom for the korekh; and if he changed the order he did not invalidate (Tur in the name of Rosh). And they bake them in order as well (Kol Bo and Avudraham). And if one of them broke, they take it for the second, for in any case they split it (Agur}.} And on the measure of a kezayit, see above siman 486.

All three: the upper for HaMotzi, the third for lechem mishneh, the broken for lechem oni; bless HaMotzi, set aside the third from his hand, bless on the broken while grasping the upper for eating matzah, bless both blessings before breaking them. Maharil and Acharonim.

baer-heitev/1:ג: (ג) In salt. And he is in writing:
baer-heitev/1:ד: (ד) HaMotzi. As above siman 472 seif 8. Magen Avraham wrote at minimum l'chatchila swallow a crushed kezayit at once; b'dieved even little by little if he does not delay between them longer than eating a peras; and likewise maror — even l'chatchila if difficult to swallow together — end.
baer-heitev/1:ה: (ה) Selecting. To the death of the es inside and do not welcome until after the first harvest, eat:
baer-heitev/1:ו: (ו) Taste. One should not soak maror beforehand in water, for it is pickled (Magen Avraham siman 473 seif 14). Chok Yaakov is lenient — see there.
baer-heitev/1:ז: (ז) Leaning. If he wishes to lean he may.
baer-heitev/1:ח: (ח) In charoset. So Bach, Maharal of Prague, Taz, Chok Yaakov, and Acharonim — dip in charoset; Magen Avraham wrote where customary it is customary.
baer-heitev/1:ט: (ט) Like Hillel. Our formula is so: Hillel when the Temple stood wrapped matza and maror and ate, etc. Taz wrote it should read wrapped Pesach, matza, and maror and ate — so Rashi and Ari. Chok Yaakov wrote now there is no Pesach so one should not mention Pesach lest speak falsehood since one has no Pesach — therefore do not change our formula — end.
baer-heitev/1:י: (י) He speaks. If he spoke he need not return and bless (Bach, Taz, Magen Avraham).
baer-heitev/2:א: (א) Vegetables. And it is good to return to the rest of the fruit of my soul’s follicles, and if he does not have vegetables, he will take another thing in his mouth. M:
baer-heitev/2:ב: (ב) haadamah. Magen Avraham wrote only if taking that type of maror fit to eat raw does one bless on it; what is not normally eaten raw like tamcha called horseradish — bless only on eating maror, not borei peri haadamah, like pepper explained siman 202 where one does not bless on it — end; see there. Chok Yaakov disagreed and wrote on all types of maror one blesses borei peri haadamah even if not eaten raw — nevertheless bless at dipping borei peri haadamah and on eating maror — see there.
baer-heitev/3:א: (א) He fulfilled. But l'chatchila he should chew until crushed then swallow, like maror; Magen Avraham.
baer-heitev/3:ב: (ב) He fulfilled. We do not say maror nullifies matza since he did not chew them together; but one who chews matza and maror together does not fulfill, for maror nowadays is d'rabbanan and matza d'oraisa, and maror is nullified by matza as in Gemara. Magen Avraham — see there.

Taz wrote that even if one did not interrupt this measure one has fulfilled, nevertheless it is mitzvah from the best to swallow a kezayit of matzah, and likewise maror when crushed at once, as stated in seif kaf gimmel and seif dalet — see there.

machatzit-hashekel/1:_: (א) He takes, etc. — nevertheless it should have stated, etc. — see siman 158 seif yud: one must intend, for washing taken for something dipped in liquid — if he reconsidered and wants to eat bread, some say he must wash again.
machatzit-hashekel/2:_: (Seif bet) And he holds them, etc. — all three from Shulchan Aruch language implies: when holding the upper and broken, on one he blesses motzi and on the second eating matzah; and since some say to bless on the whole motzi and on the broken eating matzah, and some reverse — therefore he holds both and blesses both blessings one after another (and why Taz wrote what Shulchan Aruch states 'if unable, etc., eat from motzi first' is not precise, for one does not know which is motzi); but Bach, Rashal, and Shelah wrote one must eat all three because of lechem mishneh — why should Passover night be lesser than other Yom Tov in this? — only a broken piece is also required because an impoverished person's custom is to break.
machatzit-hashekel/3:_: (סק ג) The upper one — even if split on Shabbat, as explained siman 474 one cuts at night on the lower one.
machatzit-hashekel/4:א: (א) (C.D.) As an olive tree, as a quaint as a quaint, and I will take the olives of the grove at once:
machatzit-hashekel/4:ב: (ב) (ד) Wraps all three — meaning Hillel's wrapping was Pesach, matza, and maror, for we say the swallowing chamber does not hold more than one chicken egg, and here three olives are one and a half eggs; implies he holds swallowing one olive suffices; should read for us one olive matza and maror (weak precision); though for us wrapping matza and maror as Hillel did, at minimum should eat two olives matza and maror in one gulp per view Hillel held since for us it is only stringency as below.
machatzit-hashekel/4:ג: (ג) (ד) And so in Chullin chapter 7, etc. — in my opinion this proof needs forcing; per Tosafot there no proof; per Rashi slight proof that partial live animal from outside (Rashi: cut before putting in mouth, ate each part separately) all exempt — Rashi: though all prohibitions combine within eating a peras, Rashi teaches ordinary eating is at once except prohibitions reveal law they combine within peras; but limb is novel that bones and sinews combine for kezayit.
machatzit-hashekel/5:א: (א) (c) as an empty olive. And he ate a whole brilliant in the J.C. in Reed D.D. less than his olives to greet him with a final blessing:
machatzit-hashekel/5:ב: (ב) (ה) For there is no root — therefore cannot eat with roots, for root drashot come and nullify maror mitzvah as seif 13; since must remove roots it is no longer raw as siman 204.
machatzit-hashekel/6:_: (סק ו) Without leaning — many in Gemara: maror needs no leaning because it commemorates servitude; if he leans there is no harm, for Hillel wrapped Pesach matza maror together; Pesach and matza require leaning — how did he eat maror leaning? Or b'dieved he fulfilled; regarding Hillel it is b'dieved since impossible otherwise.
machatzit-hashekel/7:_: (סק ז) And he submerges — Bach similarly: they do as Hillel and Hillel dipped in charoset; view of those who do not dip: Sages enacted only two dippings not three; those requiring dipping hold two maror dippings count as one since done from doubt to fulfill Hillel who wrapped them; Sages' view: one should not wrap.
magen-avraham/1:א: (א) He should wash his hands. And even though he washed for the vegetables, as written in siman 473, nevertheless since he will recite the Haggadah we are concerned lest he diverted his attention and touched an unclean place (Gemara). And the Mordekhai wrote that if at the first washing he intended to complete the entire meal without diverting attention he need not wash a second time, end of his words. And it appears to me that one should not intend this, so as not to nullify the enactment of the Sages who enacted washing twice on this night (Beit Yosef). And I do not know where we find this enactment, for we say: one who washed his hands at the first dipping must wash his hands at the second dipping, and the reason is written alongside: lest he diverted his attention — and if so, when he did not divert attention he need not wash. However, he needed to bless immediately at the first washing; see siman 158 seif 7 that he must intend that he washes for eating, and see there seif 2.
magen-avraham/1:ב: (ב) And he should grasp them in his hand — all three — so that there will be lechem mishneh and a broken piece because of lechem oni (Bach, Maharshal, Shelah).
magen-avraham/1:ג: (ג) The upper one — even if it split on Shabbat, so wrote in Darkei Moshe; see siman 274.
magen-avraham/1:ד: (ד) A kezayit from each. For the broken piece of HaMotzi also requires a kezayit, and so is in the Tur; see siman 167 seif 61. Darkei Moshe wrote in Terumat HaDeshen siman 139 that one must eat the kezayit together and swallow it, and so too the Beit Yosef in the name of Tosafos, end of his words — it is implied from his wording that when he swallows one kezayit in one gulp; and so too in Terumat HaDeshen there, who wrote on that which we say we wrap all three in one gulp — the Mordekhai asks how one can hold the swallowing chamber so large, for a kezayit is half an egg, and one can say that when it reaches the swallowing chamber it is crushed, and therefore one can hold so much; thus it is proven from here that one should not swallow the kezayit of matza little by little, for otherwise the question would not be difficult at all, for one could well put all three olive-bulks together in his mouth and chew them together and swallow little by little; rather the mitzvah is to swallow together, and the same applies for us for one kezayit of matza or of maror, end of his words — it is implied that he holds that when he swallows one kezayit in one gulp. And that which is written in the Shulchan Aruch that he should eat them together means that he should put them in his mouth in one gulp. And Maharil wrote that one may eat little by little provided he does not delay in his eating more than the time to eat a peras; but in seif 6 it is implied that only after the fact he has fulfilled his obligation, but l'chatchila he must eat together, and so too in Chullin chapter 7 that one must swallow together; however for maror one may rely on Maharil if it is difficult for him to swallow together; see siman 172 seif 69.
magen-avraham/1:ה: (ה) A kezayit of maror. And even if he ate the whole stalk, it is not called a stalk to fulfill with less than a kezayit (as written in siman 210), for one does not fulfill with roots (Piskei Maharai siman 245).
magen-avraham/1:ו: (ו) Without leaning. And if he ate it while leaning he has fulfilled (as is clear in the Gemara).
magen-avraham/1:ז: (ז) And he dips it in charoset. And so too Bach and Maharal of Prague and Taz, and where it is customary it is customary.
magen-avraham/1:ח: (ח) He should not speak. And if he spoke he need not return and bless again (Bach); see siman 492 seif 63: it appears to me that for this he must swallow the two olive-bulks together as stated above, unless it is difficult for him.
magen-avraham/2:א: (א) If he has no vegetables, etc. And it is good to seek other vegetables to remove himself from the dispute in the Gemara (Kesef Mishneh in Maggid Mishneh). And it appears to me that if he has no vegetables he should take something else whose blessing is Borei peri ha'adamah, even a type of pastry.
magen-avraham/2:ב: (ב) At the first dipping with Borei peri ha'adamah. It requires further study for us, since we are accustomed to take karpas for maror — if so, how do we bless on it with Borei peri ha'adamah, for it is not fit to eat while raw (as written in siman 210)? Granted, when one blesses on other vegetables with Borei peri ha'adamah it is not difficult how the karpas is discharged thereby, for one must bless on it Shehakol — one can say as some poskim write that the blessing of HaMotzi discharges it. And further it appears to me that one who eats karpas does not bless on it at all, for it is not the way to eat it as it is, as written in siman 202 regarding pepper; therefore it appears to me that if he has no other vegetables he says from the outset only the blessing on eating maror, as above.
magen-avraham/3:א: (א) If he swallowed matza he has fulfilled. But l'chatchila he must chew it, for we require the taste of matza (Rashbam). And if you ask, if so even after the fact he should not have fulfilled, as written in siman 461 seif 4 that one does not fulfill with cooked matza because the taste of matza is lacking — one can say that it is different there, for when it was cooked it is no longer in the category of matza upon it and it is as if he ate another type that is not matza; but here there is matza, only he does not sense it in his mouth; therefore he has fulfilled.
magen-avraham/3:ב: (ב) For the taste of maror is required — he should feel the bitterness in his mouth.
magen-avraham/3:ג: (ג) He has fulfilled for matza. And we do not say that maror nullifies matza since he did not chew them as one; but one who swallows matza and maror as one has not fulfilled, for maror nowadays is d'rabbanan and maror comes and nullifies matza. And with this is resolved that which they eat at first each one separately and afterward wrap them together, for it suffices when they wrap together — rather the reason is so that maror not nullify matza. And if you ask, if so let him eat matza first and afterward matza and maror — one can say that then matza would be optional and maror a d'rabbanan mitzvah, and matza would nullify matza for maror (all this is in the Gemara and Ran).
magen-avraham/4:_: Without intention. Even though mitzvot require intention, as written in siman 60 seif 4 — in matters of eating it is different, for behold he ate and enjoyed it; and for this reason even if he knew it was matza and did not want to eat and they forced him to eat he has fulfilled, in the Beit Yosef; see siman 204 seif 8 and siman 196.
magen-avraham/6:_: Between one eating and its fellow. It is not precise — rather he must not delay from the beginning of the first eating until the end of the last eating more than the time to eat a peras, as written in siman 612.
magen-avraham/7:א: (א) On the first night. And nevertheless he is obligated to eat bread every day, only he fulfills with rich matza (Ran chapter 2 of Sukkah); see siman 188 seif 7, and see siman 471 seif 2.
magen-avraham/7:ב: (ב) From an issaron. Darkei Moshe wrote that Mahariv wrote that if he has many children so that the measure of challah is not sufficient for him, it is permitted to knead two doughs less than the measure and combine them; and Maharil forbids unless he limits himself to take an issaron, end of Darkei Moshe's words. And it requires further study, for Mahariv wrote to combine them at the time of challah and to make from both of them three matzot so that he can give a kezayit to each, and thereby there is no prohibition at all; and so too in Hagahot Semak, and so one should practice; see siman 456.
magen-avraham/7:ג: (ג) He fulfills with a kezayit. See siman 482, and see there — not for its own sake.

mishnah-berurah/1:ט: (ט) (c) As an olive from each one, the Prussian must certainly be called the Daa olive tree, and there is no eating less than an olive tree, but the non-citem of the pelvis clarifies even less than the olives and radars in a single sign of food. And the last cheque has only to put the two olives at once and to crash, but it is not obliged to swallow at once, but rather to be planted as an olive equivalent One daughter and then the rest will be swallowed up, and even if the olive swallow is a little bit, it is not that the food is digested until the end of eating a reward:
mishnah-berurah/1:י: (10) (j) Of the one who spends first - it is the supreme complement that the main part of the judgment arose when the blessing of the spender and not what was eaten between the blessing of eating matzah and the eating of the slice since it came for the purpose of that olive, that is, for the purpose of the blessing of the spender, one must also bless the kozit of the slice. mishnah-berurah/1:ל: (ל) (b) As a snoring olive, and even eating a whole platter with the leaf, it did not come out of everything that does not have any olives
mishnah-berurah/1:מ: (מ) (g) And we invested all – in order to kill ars inside it. There are places that are not used to the entire sink, but in the confusion of some:
mishnah-berurah/1:נ: (נ) (d) And we shall eat without the reason - that he remembers slavery and VAT if he wants to eat for the reason:

mishnah-berurah/1:ש: (ש) Like Hillel — and our formula in the Haggadah: so Hillel did when the Temple stood, etc. — he wrapped matzah and maror and ate them together; and some wrote it should read: he wrapped Pesach, matzah, and maror.

mishnah-berurah/2:ב: (ב) For the sake of eating a snoring, it is not like the rest of the time to eat without a blessing, and to bless the eating of another, which is already filled with a certain amount of food that has not been eaten from it before, and that it is not possible to eat it from the place of light, and that it is not to be eaten Other bees:
mishnah-berurah/2:ג: (ג) (כז) And at second dipping he dips it, etc. — this is eating maror after kezayit matza; he dips it in charoset since this maror he eats to fulfill maror mitzvah, requiring charoset dipping like ordinary maror; must eat kezayit for this reason too.
mishnah-berurah/2:ד: (ד) Without a blessing, he came out in his mouth and eats a snorkel of the first. And the knowledge of a lot of stops is shared by it and its friend Piy is better at feeding the first snoring to keep the snoring of the wood so that we are blessed and so on and so on, and the friend must eat so as olives and immerse themselves in order to make them free. And the second ventilation that eats without blessing is for the sake of a charcoal and is not obliged to eat as an olive, and should not be immersed in the jackpot or the salt of the sages, and shall not be used for the purpose of the matter The printer:

turei-zahav/1:א: (א) He grasps them in his hand. The reason: some poskim bless HaMotzi on the whole and eating matzah on the broken lechem oni; some hold the reverse — therefore he grasps two in his hand and blesses both blessings, then breaks from the whole. Tur wrote 'he takes the plate,' etc.: meaning one should not remove the whole matza from the plate and grasp it, for then it separates from the third matza and we require lechem mishneh as every Yom Tov; rather they remain on the plate and he brings them near, or takes all three matzot in hand, places his hand on them, then removes the whole and breaks, then breaks from the broken; Rashal wrote first bless HaMotzi and break the whole without fully breaking it first, then grasp the second and bless on eating matzah and break from both — end; I do not know this breaking first without fully breaking; also why divide blessings HaMotzi on whole and eating matzah on broken — he holds one view; but Tur's meaning is fulfill both views, say two blessings consecutively while still on the plate, then break them sequentially; so Tur siman 486 that breaking should be as one.
turei-zahav/1:ב: (ב) He eats them leaning together. Because both blessings relate to each other; even if he had only one matza, we do not make bundled mitzvot — therefore he takes one matza per blessing so eating is as one, as if truly one matza. Maharal of Prague challenged: we say chapter HaIsh Mekadesh whatever is not sequential even in one gulp does not apply — I did not understand the question, for here both are truly one body as explained, unlike HaIsh Mekadesh. This also resolves Maaseh Choshev: why kezayit for HaMotzi — answered siman 167 we do not require kezayit for HaMotzi eating; no question, for here both blessings fall on two matzot without division, both as one eating. One could say: why two kezayit — one suffices from both; answer: since doing so to fulfill both views, each bears name HaMotzi and eating matzah — must eat kezayit from each for eating matzah; otherwise Tur brought first bless HaMotzi on whole and eating matzah on broken yet eat kezayit from each — requires study; also per view that enactment is whatever he eats at that time both blessings apply as one — if he eats kezayit from one and less from other, eating unequal — at start two mitzvot, at end one — as I explained.
turei-zahav/1:ג: (ג) He eats the HaMotzi one first. So Tur siman 486. It appears this applies only to first Tur view blessing HaMotzi on whole and broken for eating matzah — then we know which is HaMotzi and it precedes if cannot eat together; per later words blessing both together — no distinction which is for matza or HaMotzi, therefore Shulchan Aruch and Tur should not write this per that view; only since whole is before him first lest violate mitzvot he eats it first; therefore if he removes broken from hand and only broken remains in hand he should not set it aside but take broken from whole — for this too violates mitzvot in my view.
turei-zahav/1:ד: (ד) And submerge it entirely in charoset. Due to kapa — meaning a worm species inside dies in charoset.
turei-zahav/1:ה: (ה) Third matza. To fulfill one mitzvah in it.
turei-zahav/1:ו: (ו) And dip in charoset. Hillel dipped in charoset, for his main maror mitzvah was here — Hillel held 'on matzot and maror they shall eat it' means all together; Rabanan hold each separately; if fulfilling both views why not take charoset for wrapping? Perhaps Rama brings Avi Ezri in Tur. Tur wrote Rashi and Rosh agreed to dip in charoset; so Rashal ruled; Maharal of Prague practiced; though written in customs and Rama, I saw custom not to dip wrapping in charoset; Maaseh Choshev wrote not to practice so — correct to dip wrapping in charoset too; Avi Ezri: we find only two dippings not three; Rama end siman 476 — one can say two charoset dippings count as one, for we do not do so except from doubt.
turei-zahav/1:ז: (ז) So blessing on eating matzah applies, etc. Meaning for Hillel this is main mitzvah here, therefore related to eating matzah blessing; appears interruption only in unnecessary speech, but necessary matters like 'take wrap' are not interruption; seemingly if he spoke between blessing and wrapping he must return and bless HaMotzi and eating matzah like HaMotzi rest of year siman 167 seif 6; here too must fulfill Hillel for we say in Gemara now law not stated like either — act with stringencies of both; Tur wrote one wishing optimal mitzvah should not speak until wrapping — implies b'dieved no need return and bless.
turei-zahav/2:_: And on eating maror. For they said bless on eating maror the second time — how bless when already filled from first? We do not bless final blessing on maror — reason explained siman 473 in dispute R' Yehuda and Rashbam.
turei-zahav/3:_: For maror taste is required — in mouth he should feel bitterness, commemoration of bitterness; if he does not feel, no commemoration; not so matza — though taste required, if he cooked does not fulfill siman 461; there we do not require feeling matza taste in mouth, for Torah did not command feeling, only eating alone; swallowing is called eating. Levush expanded on this difficulty and Lechem Mishneh's words. In formula zecher lemikdash keHillel one can say he wrapped Pesach matza maror — so Rashi in Gemara on Hillel who wrapped at once, i.e. Pesach with them.
turei-zahav/5:_: (5) Obligated to eat after he is healed. We do not say since pushed off it is pushed off, since time still applies and it is not compensation; do not challenge from Yoreh De'ah siman 396 minor who grew during mourning days exempt — as I wrote there in my explanation — see there.
turei-zahav/6:_: (6) Like half olive, etc. In Tur HaTov siman 139 written: optimal mitzvah to swallow together entire kezayit matza and likewise maror when crushed.
turei-zahav/7:_: (7) If one of them broke. Meaning even if the third broke, due to precedence for mitzvah he should not bake another.
